rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important first step is to establish a clear, interpretable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible RNA-only configuration: no image processing, no learned encoder, single profile, no aggregation or fusion. It gives a performance floor against which every other design choice (image modality, learned encoders, multiprofile, aggregation, fusion) can be measured. It is also computationally cheap, leaving budget for more complex experiments later. Testing this baseline first reduces uncertainty about the RNA signal strength and the cost of added complexity, and provides the reference point needed to interpret all subsequent comparisons in the remaining 9 experiments.

With only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality provides complementary or superior signal. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest direct comparison to config_001: same profile setting (singleprofile), same structural simplicity (no aggregation/fusion), and a standard pretrained encoder. This establishes the two unimodal baselines. If image_only substantially outperforms rna_only, it signals strong visual signal and justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion configs. If it underperforms, it tells us to focus on RNA encoder/aggregation improvements. Resolving the modality question early is the highest-value uncertainty reduction given 8 remaining experiments, as it determines whether the multimodal configs (configs 016–051) are worth testing at all.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 acc while image (ResNet50) is weak at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the PCA linear projection is the bottleneck or whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi) can extract more discriminative signal from the same RNA data. This experiment tests config_004 (RNA-only, single profile, scvi_n200), which is a clean single-variable comparison to config_001—only the encoder changes. If scvi substantially improves over PCA, we know learned representations are critical and should prioritize the best encoder for all downstream multimodal experiments; if it is comparable or worse, PCA is sufficient and we can redirect remaining budget toward multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments left, resolving the encoder question early is the highest-information, lowest-risk step before committing to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.520) clearly outperforms pca_n2000 (0.485) in singleprofile RNA-only, and image-only is very weak (0.208), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: we have no data on whether multiprofile adds value over singleprofile for the best encoder. This experiment (scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool) isolates the effect of multiprofile with the simplest aggregation on top of the current best encoder, directly testing whether capturing multiple profiles improves on the 0.520 baseline. It is the best use of experiment 4 because it exploits the strongest encoder evidence while reducing uncertainty about a key design axis (profile setting) before committing remaining budget to more complex multimodal or transformer-aggregation configurations.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over its singleprofile counterpart (0.520). The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation could further improve over avgpool for the same encoder and profile setting. config_006 changes only the aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) while holding rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200 constant, giving a clean single-variable comparison. This is the best use of experiment 5 because it directly exploits the strongest evidence, isolates the aggregation effect, and the result will inform whether transformer aggregation is worth carrying into multimodal configurations in the remaining 5 experiments.

Evidence: The current best (config_006, rna_only/multiprofile/scvi_n200/transformer, 0.6530) shows that multiprofile + transformer aggregation is the dominant driver of performance, and scvi_n200 outperformed pca_n2000 in single-profile (0.52 vs 0.48). However, scgpt has not yet been tested, leaving uncertainty about whether a pre-trained RNA foundation model can surpass scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting. Question: Does scgpt provide a meaningfully better RNA representation than scvi_n200 when paired with multiprofile + transformer aggregation? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_006 (only the encoder changes). Why this is the best use of experiment 6: It directly challenges the current best with a minimal change, isolates the encoder effect, and its outcome will determine whether the remaining 4 experiments should build multimodal configs around scgpt or scvi_n200—resolving a key design choice before committing budget to more complex multimodal combinations.

The current best is config_006 (RNA-only, scVI n200, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653. The key open question is whether multimodal fusion can improve upon this. Image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208), so the critical test is whether fusing it with the strong RNA signal helps or hurts. config_033 takes the best-validated RNA stack (scVI n200 + multiprofile + transformer) and adds ResNet50 image features with weighted fusion, which can learn to down-weight the weaker image modality. This isolates the fusion effect while keeping all other design choices at their empirically best settings. The result will determine whether to spend remaining experiments exploring stronger image encoders (ViT-L) in multimodal mode or to confirm RNA-only as the ceiling and explore minor RNA-side variations.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image encoder may not be extracting useful features, limiting the multimodal gain (~6 pts over RNA-only). config_039 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical to config_033 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted fusion), cleanly isolating the image encoder effect. A stronger visual backbone could provide more complementary spatial/morphological information to the RNA modality, potentially pushing accuracy above 0.713. This is the highest-value single-variable test: if ViT helps, it confirms the image encoder was the bottleneck; if it doesn't, the RNA modality dominates and further image-side changes are low-priority. With 2 experiments remaining after this, a positive result would allow one final refinement, while a null result would confirm config_033 as the best achievable configuration.

The best result so far is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. The only fusion type tested in the multimodal setting is 'weighted.' Config_038 is identical to config_039 except it uses 'concat' fusion, directly isolating the effect of fusion strategy while holding all other parameters (RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation, profile setting) constant. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison available to determine whether the current best configuration can be further improved or whether weighted fusion is already optimal. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most promising unexplored axis (fusion type) on the strongest base configuration maximizes the chance of either finding a new best or confirming the current best is near-optimal.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. All top-performing components (scvi_n200 RNA encoder, vit_l image encoder, multiprofile, weighted fusion) are already in place. The one untested single-variable variant is config_037, which swaps transformer aggregation for avgpool while keeping all other settings identical to the best. In the RNA-only setting, transformer vs avgpool showed only a ~0.003 gap (0.6530 vs 0.6501), suggesting the choice may be noise-level. In the multimodal context, the interaction between aggregation and the image pathway is untested—avgpool could theoretically reduce overfitting or noise introduced by the transformer when fusing two modalities. As the final experiment, this is the most targeted exploitation step: a single-variable change from the current best that has a small but non-zero chance of matching or exceeding 0.7250, while also clarifying whether the transformer aggregation advantage seen in RNA-only transfers to the multimodal setting.
